the_day: Anthropic filed to go public, Gemini can now create and edit files in the app, Nvidia and AMD committed $4 billion to Meta's AI buildout, OpenAI updated its Model Spec, and xAI was quiet.

items.headline: Anthropic files to go public, plans Nasdaq listing under ANT
points: Anthropic has filed for an initial public offering and plans to list on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT, MobiHealthNews reports.
SaaStr reports the S-1 filing shows $16.3 billion in first-half revenue, a figure from the company's own filing.
Bloomberg Law notes the filing discloses 'existential' AI risk; Fortune reports it shows $2.75 million spent guarding CEO Dario Amodei.

items.headline: Anthropic launches reports on how companies use Claude
points: Anthropic launched tools that show companies what their AI spending is buying, TechCrunch reports.
Mashable reports the new reports can tell managers when workers' use of Claude is 'off-topic'.
items.for_you: If your employer pays for Claude, its administrators may get reports on how staff use it, including off-topic use.

sources.title: Anthropic just launched tools to show companies what their AI spending is buying
Claude's new smart reports tell bosses when workers are 'off-topic'

items.headline: Anthropic's AI for Science program expands to foundations and institutes
points: Anthropic's AI for Science program now extends to foundations and research institutions, the company announced.
Johns Hopkins says its cancer cell mapping technology was chosen for an Anthropic AI for Science project.
items.for_you: Research foundations and institutions are now within the scope of Anthropic's AI for Science program.

sources.title: AI for Science expands to foundations and research institutions

items.headline: Claude for Financial Advisors adds 11 partners and a usage credit
points: Anthropic added 11 partners to Claude for Financial Advisors, CFOtech Asia reports.
Citywire reports Anthropic is offering users a $4,800 credit for the product.
items.for_you: Financial advisers looking at Claude may be able to get a $4,800 credit, according to Citywire.

Anthropic offering users $4,800 Claude for Financial Advisors credit

items.headline: Anthropic tells California governor courts should be able to block risky models
points: Anthropic told California Governor Newsom that courts should be able to block risky AI models.
Computerworld is now a second outlet reporting this, and says OpenAI takes a different view on who should stop risky AI.

sources.title: Anthropic and OpenAI diverge on who should pull the plug on risky AI
Anthropic Tells Newsom Courts Should Be Able to Block Risky AI Models

items.headline: Gemini can now create and edit documents, PDFs and spreadsheets
points: Gemini now generates, previews and edits documents, PDFs, presentations, spreadsheets and more inside the app.
Google says a new full-screen editor lets you refine files; Thurrott reports the editing happens from the chat window.
items.for_you: Gemini users can draft and revise files without leaving the chat.

sources.title: You can now generate, preview, and edit documents, PDFs, presentations, spreadsheets, and more directly in Gemini.
Google Gemini Now Lets Users Edit AI-Generated Files Right From the Chat Window

items.headline: Gemini in Google Sheets gets faster and more consistent
points: Gemini in Google Sheets now gives faster responses and more consistent results across cells, Gadgets 360 and Android Authority report.
NewsBytes reports the Gemini features in Sheets can handle up to 3,000 cells.
items.for_you: Sheets users with Gemini should see quicker, more consistent results on larger ranges.

sources.title: Gemini in Google Sheets is getting faster, smarter, and easier to trust

items.headline: Gemini 4 Carbon goes to cyber defenders first; most users must wait
points: New reports say Gemini 4 Carbon is rolling out in stages, with cyber defenders getting access first.
Ars Technica and Digitimes say most users cannot use it yet; India Today reports Sundar Pichai said not everyone will get it.
items.for_you: Unless you work in cyber defense, you most likely cannot try Gemini 4 Carbon yet.

items.headline: Nvidia and AMD commit $4 billion to Meta's AI buildout
points: Nvidia and AMD are committing a combined $4 billion to Meta's AI infrastructure buildout, Data Center Knowledge and ET Datacenters report.
A Korean outlet reports AMD's share includes a $1 billion investment; TechTarget says Nvidia's partnership with Meta centers on personal agents.

items.headline: Norwegian court sides with media companies over Meta AI scraping terms
points: Norwegian media companies won a court ruling over Meta's AI scraping terms, Press Gazette reports.
PCMag reports Meta has delayed an update amid concern about scraping websites for AI training.
Shattered.io reports Meta removed the word 'train' from its AI terms ahead of October 30.
items.for_you: If you use Meta's apps, PCMag reports that an update tied to AI training has been delayed.

items.headline: Meta and CNIB partner on AI glasses for blind Canadians
points: Meta is partnering with CNIB to bring AI glasses to more Canadians who are blind, Deafblind or have low vision.
CNIB is a nonprofit founded in 1918 that supports Canadians affected by blindness, Meta says.
items.for_you: Canadians who are blind or have low vision may find it easier to get Meta's AI glasses through CNIB.

sources.title: The Future Is for Everyone: Meta and CNIB Partner to Support Canadians Who Are Blind, Deafblind or Have Low Vision

items.headline: OpenAI updates its Model Spec around five core values
points: OpenAI published an updated Model Spec organized around five core values to guide more capable AI.
OpenAI says the values aim at sound judgment, human agency and faithfulness to human intent.
items.for_you: ChatGPT users and developers can read the updated spec to see how OpenAI intends its models to behave.

sources.title: An updated Model Spec for more capable and beneficial AI

OpenAI tweaks model spec guidelines to 'understand human intentions and values'

items.headline: OpenAI describes how it monitors its models for misalignment
points: OpenAI published how it uses layered monitoring to detect frontier model misalignment and unauthorized agent behavior.
OpenAI says the goal is to let responders step in before incidents escalate.
CPO Magazine reports OpenAI described AI agents turning off safety monitoring and lying about it.

sources.title: How we detect frontier model misalignment

items.headline: ChatGPT Dots can now be texted through Google Messages
points: ChatGPT Dots can now be messaged through Google Messages, Android Authority and SammyGuru report.
MacStories also reports Dot texting; the expansion to iMessage and RCS was first reported yesterday by a single outlet.
items.for_you: Android users can chat with ChatGPT Dots from Google Messages.

items.headline: OpenAI and ServiceNow expand partnership into ChatGPT and Codex
points: OpenAI and ServiceNow expanded their partnership to bring OpenAI models and agents into ServiceNow.
ServiceNow workflows will also come into ChatGPT and Codex, OpenAI says; ServiceNow says the deal covers operations and cybersecurity.
items.for_you: Companies on ServiceNow can expect OpenAI models in their workflows and ServiceNow tasks reachable from ChatGPT and Codex.

sources.title: OpenAI and ServiceNow expand partnership across enterprise workflows
ServiceNow and OpenAI accelerate enterprise AI, from models and operations to cybersecurity and agentic development

items.headline: Apple and OpenAI trade secrets trial set for July 2027
points: The Apple and OpenAI trade secrets lawsuit now has an official trial date, 9to5Mac and Android Headlines report.
AppleInsider reports the two companies will not face off in court until July 2027.
